headline: Across my 37 items the three-method vocabulary (sv/smoke/grill) is not a "cooking method" vocabulary at all — it is a HEAT-SOURCE vocabulary, and it is missing the two heat sources that actually dominate this domain: a pot of water/steam (9 of 15 seafood items are primarily boiled or steamed) and a dry oven (every whole bird). It is also missing a whole cooking MEDIUM — fat — which is the defining constraint of both waterfowl categories and the literal name of two catalog items (שוק ברווז קונפי, שוק אווז קונפי) that today can only be offered sous-vide, smoke or grill. Beyond the vocabulary gap there is a live wrong answer: the six items with no `doneness` entry (n=3 שווארמה, 43 הודו שלם, 44 אווז שלם, 45 שוק אווז, 46 ברווז שלם, 47 שוק ברווז) fall through methodRules' final "collagen/long cuts" branch, so a 6 kg whole turkey DEFAULTS to sous-vide and roasting/grilling it alone is marked invalid — and five bivalve/crab items carry `svt=0` yet still default to `['sv','smoke']`. Finally the model has no pre-cook and no post-cook stage, so brine, dry-brine, cure, thaw, air-dry/pellicle, score, and tenderise — days of clock time in an orchestrator app — are all smuggled into the `rub`, `mid`, `sear` and `somid` prose fields where the engine cannot see them.

categories.notesOnOurModel: All 6 chicken items carry a `doneness` entry so they land in the steak-like branch (allowed sv/smoke/grill, default sv+smoke, every combo legal). Two structural failures. (1) The bird's two-target problem is inexpressible: n=38 עוף שלם ספאצ'קוק has ONE tgt (74) and ONE doneness scale ('dark'), but a whole bird's breast wants ~62-65°C and its thigh wants 74-80°C — that divergence IS the reason spatchcocking exists, and the app cannot say it. (2) `mid:'ייבוש עור'` appears on 4 of the 6 items as a bare label; skin-drying is a real stage with a clock (uncovered fridge, hours) and equipment (wire rack + sheet pan), not a note. The single most common domestic method for a whole chicken — a 200-220°C dry oven — cannot be selected at all, even though `oven` is an owned equipment category with `fan` and `steam` props already modelled, and the grill already carries a `rotisserie` boolean prop (app.js:89) that nothing can consume.

methods.whatItProduces: Deep smoke penetration, mahogany colour, rendered but RUBBERY skin below ~150°C — the classic low-and-slow poultry skin complaint. Juicy dark meat; breast dries if held long.
methods.equipment: מעשנה (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled. What is lost is the temperature distinction: `smt:120-150` vs `sot:130-150` is a single number, so the app cannot express "smoke at 110°C for flavour then blast to 200°C for skin".
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C / 165°F instantaneous for all poultry — this is our existing `safe:74` and it is correctly sourced.

methods.whatItProduces: Hard char, Maillard crust, crisp rendered skin on wings/thighs; flare-ups from dripping fat; breast overcooks before skin crisps.
methods.equipment: גריל (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled, but conflated with indirect grilling under one token.

methods.whatItProduces: Convection-oven behaviour inside a kettle: even cooking, crisp skin at 180-200°C dome temp, no flare-up. This is how a spatchcock chicken is actually cooked on a kettle.
methods.equipment: גריל with lid + 2 heat zones — the grill `lid` bool and `zones` capKey ALREADY exist in app.js:80-86
methods.whyItMatters: The most-used real technique for whole birds on a grill is unnameable. Worse: app.js:1168 already writes advice about "עישון בגריל עקיף (2-zone)" as free text — the concept is in the copy but not in the vocabulary.
methods.safetyNote: No new safety value; USDA FSIS 74°C endpoint unchanged.

methods.whatItProduces: Dry radiant+convective heat, 190-230°C. Even browning, crisp skin if the surface is dry, no smoke flavour. The default domestic method for a whole chicken and for parts.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED equipment category, app.js:91) — with `fan` (convection) and `maxC` props already modelled
methods.whyItMatters: We own the oven, model its area, max temp, fan and steam — and no cut can select it. A user with an oven and no smoker is told their gear cannot cook a chicken.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C. Convection (`fan:true`) shortens time and typically drops set temp ~20°C — that relationship needs a citable source before we compute with it: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Continuous rotation = continuous self-basting. The most even skin in the domain — uniform bronze, fully rendered, no flip, no dry side. Fat drips away rather than pooling. Whole birds only.
methods.equipment: ערכת רוטיסרי on the grill — the `rotisserie` bool prop ALREADY EXISTS at app.js:89, tier 'pro'. Plus a drip pan (`drippan` token exists).
methods.whyItMatters: We ask the user whether they own a rotisserie, store the answer, and then never use it. That is inert-shipment: a captured capability with no consumer.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C. Motor weight rating is a real spec (a 6 kg turkey overloads a light chicken motor) — no citable consumer figure: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Bird upright: fat drains down the carcass, all skin surfaces face the heat, thighs sit closest to the fire (which is where you want them). Even skin, no soggy underside.
methods.equipment: מעמד עוף אנכי (~₪40-150) or a beer-can
methods.whyItMatters: A cheap, common technique. Note the popular claim that the liquid steams the bird is disputed by AmazingRibs/Serious Eats — the real benefit is geometry and drainage. We should ship the geometry claim, not the steam claim.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C; the cavity liquid never boils in most tests — do not imply it pasteurizes anything: requires research if we make any claim.

methods.whatItProduces: Absolute doneness control, edge-to-edge; breast at 62-65°C stays juicy where an oven would dry it. But produces FLABBY, unrenderable skin that must be removed or aggressively re-crisped.
methods.equipment: סו-ויד + ואקום (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled. The skin consequence is not — the app offers sv+grill without warning that a 2-minute sear cannot rescue sous-vide chicken skin.

methods.whatItProduces: Top-down radiant blast. The dedicated skin-crisping FINISH after any gentle cook (sous-vide, low smoke, braise). 3-6 minutes, no interior effect.
methods.equipment: תנור with a top element, or a salamander; a `torch` (owned token) is the small-item substitute
methods.whyItMatters: The specific answer to the skin-crisping problem across the whole poultry+waterfowl group, and we have no way to name it.

methods.whatItProduces: ~120°C wet heat. Thighs/drumsticks/leg quarters to fall-apart shreddable in 12-20 min instead of 2 hours. Zero browning, zero skin — a texture route, not a flavour route.
methods.equipment: סיר לחץ / אינסטנט-פוט (~₪250-800) — NOT owned, standard consumer kit
methods.whyItMatters: The fastest route to shredded chicken and to stock. Also the enabler for a pressure-then-char two-stage.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C endpoint still applies. Pressure-vessel operating pressure/temp claims: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: 170-190°C oil. Uniform shatter-crisp exterior in minutes; the canonical wing method and a real whole-bird method.
methods.equipment: מטגנת / סיר כבד + 2-3 ל' שמן + מדחום שמן (owned `probe` can serve)
methods.whyItMatters: Wings (n=39) are in the catalog and their single most common preparation is unavailable.
methods.safetyNote: Whole-bird deep frying is the highest-consequence operation in this whole report (oil displacement fire from a partially frozen bird). Do NOT ship it without USDA FSIS / NFPA turkey-frying guidance quoted verbatim: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Small high-velocity convection oven. Wings and thighs crisp in 20-25 min with no oil bath; drier result than deep-fry, far less mess.
methods.equipment: אייר פרייר (~₪250-700)
methods.whyItMatters: Extremely common consumer kit; for wings and drumsticks it is the everyday method the app pretends does not exist.

methods.whatItProduces: Full-contact conduction on a flat surface. Boneless thigh skin-down under a weight → uniformly crisp, flat, glass-like skin — better than a grate, which only contacts in stripes.
methods.equipment: 'פלנצ׳ה / פלטה' is ALREADY a grill `type` in app.js:80, or a cast-iron griddle (~₪150-600)
methods.whyItMatters: We model the hardware as a grill type but the method behaves nothing like a grate: no flare-up, no char stripes, full contact. Treating it as 'grill' gives wrong advice.

methods.whatItProduces: PROCESS STAGE, not a heat method. Salt+water 4-12h: adds water weight, raises the overcook tolerance, seasons throughout. Costs: diluted flavour and a WETTER skin that resists crisping.
methods.equipment: דלי/כלי כבישה + מקום במקרר (~₪30-100) + a scale for the salt %
methods.whyItMatters: Currently hidden in `rub` as the word 'כבישה' with no duration, no salt ratio, no vessel, no fridge-space claim. The work plan cannot schedule a 12-hour stage it cannot see.
methods.safetyNote: Brining must happen at refrigeration temperature — a bucket on the counter is a time/temperature abuse. Cite USDA FSIS cold-holding: requires research for the verbatim clause.

methods.whatItProduces: PROCESS STAGE. Salt only, uncovered in the fridge 12-72h. Draws moisture out, it dissolves the salt, the brine reabsorbs — deep seasoning AND a dried surface, which is the single best predictor of crisp skin. Strictly better than wet brine for skin.
methods.equipment: רשת + תבנית + מקום פתוח במקרר (~₪50-150) + משקל
methods.whyItMatters: The highest-leverage, lowest-cost technique in the entire poultry domain and it is not in our model at all.

categories.notesOnOurModel: Four of the five carry `doneness` and behave like chicken. The fifth and largest, n=43 הודו שלם (6 kg), has NO doneness entry and therefore falls into methodRules' final collagen branch: default `['sv','smoke']`, `needsCookFor:'grill'`, `invalid:[['grill']]`. The app's out-of-the-box recommendation for a whole 6 kg turkey is to sous-vide it, and it forbids roasting it. Sous-vide of a 6 kg whole bird is not a real technique at consumer scale — no domestic bath or vacuum bag takes it. n=3 שווארמה is also doneness-less and lands in the same branch, yet its true method is a vertical rotisserie which MAKE_COOK already names for the MAKE ('תנור/רוטיסרי', app.js:3717) while the CUT cannot select it.

methods.whatItProduces: The default whole-turkey method worldwide. 160-180°C dry heat, breast shielded, 3-4h. Even browning, crisp skin, no smoke.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED) — but a 6 kg bird tests the `areaCm2` spec we already model
methods.whyItMatters: For the single most iconic item in the catalog, the normal method is unavailable and the offered default is sous-vide.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C in the thickest part of the thigh, not touching bone.

methods.whatItProduces: Backbone out, bird flattened: roughly halves the cook time and collapses the breast/thigh endpoint gap because both now sit in one plane. Uniformly crisp skin over the whole top surface.
methods.equipment: מספרי עוף / סכין + תבנית רחבה; תנור או גריל עקיף
methods.whyItMatters: We encode spatchcock as an item NAME for chicken (n=38) and not at all for turkey. It is a PREP TRANSFORM that changes geometry, cook time and target structure — modelling it as a distinct item cannot scale (every bird × every transform).

methods.whatItProduces: PROCESS STAGE. For a 6 kg bird this is a 2-3 DAY commitment that must be on the work plan. Deep seasoning + a bone-dry skin.
methods.equipment: רשת + תבנית + significant open fridge space; משקל for the salt %
methods.whyItMatters: Our n=43 `rub` field literally reads 'כבישה+חמאת עשבים+מלח' — a multi-day stage compressed into a seasoning string. For an ORCHESTRATOR app this is the most schedule-distorting omission in my whole domain.
methods.safetyNote: Refrigerated throughout. Salt percentage by weight is the safety-adjacent number and we should cite one — requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: PROCESS STAGE with no culinary outcome and enormous schedule impact: a frozen 6 kg turkey needs multiple days in the fridge.
methods.equipment: מקרר with the space; nothing else
methods.whyItMatters: We already store `kg` on every item — the arithmetic is available and unused. A user who buys a frozen turkey two days before the cookout is going to fail, and the app will not warn them.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS publishes refrigerator-thaw time per unit weight (commonly cited as ~24h per 2-2.3 kg) and prohibits counter thawing. Get the FSIS text verbatim: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Even self-basting for a large bird; superb skin. But 6 kg on a spit needs a rated motor and counterweight.
methods.equipment: ערכת רוטיסרי (the `rotisserie` prop exists) + a heavy-duty motor
methods.whyItMatters: Also the ONLY correct method for n=3 שווארמה תלויה — a vertical spit. That item's whole identity is a method we do not have.

methods.whatItProduces: Covered vessel, liquid, 150-160°C, 2-3h. Collagen to gelatin; falling-off-the-bone turkey legs and wings with a sauce as a by-product. No crust unless finished uncovered.
methods.equipment: סיר ברזל יצוק / תבנית מכוסה + תנור (OWNED)
methods.whyItMatters: n=42 שוק הודו (tgt 85°C) and n=68 כנפי הודו are collagen cuts. Braising gets them there in a third the time of a 3h smoke and yields a sauce. This is the owner's named gap and turkey legs are its clearest case.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C is the safety floor; 82-88°C is the TEXTURE target — the app already distinguishes `safe` from `tgt`, so the schema is ready.

methods.whatItProduces: Turkey legs/wings shreddable in ~25 min. No browning.
methods.equipment: סיר לחץ (~₪250-800), not owned
methods.whyItMatters: The fast substitute for braise; also the route to turkey stock from the carcass.

methods.whatItProduces: Smoked turkey — a genuinely great product; pink smoke ring under the skin, deep flavour, but soft skin unless finished hot.
methods.equipment: מעשנה (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled and appropriate.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C. Large-bird low-temperature smoking has a slow-warming risk profile; the 4-hour 4-60°C rule is the relevant control — cite FSIS verbatim: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Breast and legs cooked as separate items to separate targets (breast 63-65°C, legs 82-85°C), then reassembled on the platter. The only technique that gets BOTH right on a large bird.
methods.equipment: סכין פריסה + קרש (both owned tokens) + two cooking positions
methods.whyItMatters: For a 6 kg bird this is what a professional actually does, and our one-item-one-target schema cannot represent it at all. It also has a scheduling shape (two parallel cooks) that the orchestrator would love.

methods.whatItProduces: A whole turkey in ~45 min; extraordinarily crisp, moist breast.
methods.equipment: מטגנת הודו ייעודית 30-40 ל' + מבער גז (~₪600-1500)
methods.whyItMatters: A famous method the app cannot mention.
methods.safetyNote: HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE item in this report. Oil-volume displacement, fully-thawed-only, outdoors-only, never on a deck. Do not ship without USDA FSIS and NFPA guidance quoted: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Not a method — a second thermal mass inside the bird with its own, HIGHER, effective risk and a slower heating curve.
methods.equipment: none beyond the roast
methods.whyItMatters: If a user stuffs the bird, every time estimate we produce is wrong and the safety endpoint moves to the stuffing.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS requires the STUFFING itself to reach 74°C / 165°F. This is a safety-relevant number with a named authority and we have no field to put it in: requires research to quote the FSIS clause verbatim.

categories.notesOnOurModel: All three waterfowl problems in one category. n=9 חזה אווז has doneness (mr default 57°C) and behaves like a steak. n=44 אווז שלם (4.5 kg) and n=45 שוק אווז (קונפי) have NO doneness and fall to the collagen branch — so a whole goose defaults to sous-vide+smoke and cannot be roasted alone, and an item whose Hebrew name is literally 'קונפי' is offered sous-vide, smoke and grill but not confit. The `mid` field carries the real knowledge as prose — n=44 says 'ניקוז שומן' and `somid` says 'דקירת עור+ניקוז' — meaning the engine knows the words for fat-drainage and skin-piercing but has no stage to execute them. The saved-fat yield (a goose gives 0.5-1 kg of schmaltz) is a real product of the cook with nowhere to live.

methods.whatItProduces: Salt-cure 12-24h, rinse, fully submerge in rendered fat, hold 80-90°C for 2-4h. Meat becomes silky and falls off the bone WITHOUT drying, because fat cannot carry water away. Then chilled and stored under the fat cap; finished crisp in a hot pan or oven.
methods.equipment: סיר ברזל יצוק עמוק + 1.5-2 ק"ג שומן אווז/ברווז + תנור that holds 80-90°C accurately (OWNED oven, if its low-end control is good)
methods.whyItMatters: An item NAMED confit cannot be confited. Our `svt:80/svh:8-10` is a sous-vide APPROXIMATION of confit (bag + fat + 80°C) which is a legitimate modern technique — but the app never says so, cannot express the cure, the fat quantity, the fat as an input, or the store-under-fat preservation step which is the historical POINT of the dish.
methods.safetyNote: Confit's traditional preservation claim (months under fat) rests on the salt cure + fat seal + cold storage, not on the cook. I have NO primary source for a safe cure ratio, hold time, or refrigerated shelf life: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: PREP + METHOD in one. Crosshatch the fat cap without cutting the meat; start SKIN-DOWN in a COLD dry pan; low heat 12-18 min; pour off the rendered fat repeatedly; flip for 1-2 min. Outcome: glass-thin crackling skin over MR meat, and 100-200 ml of pure fat as a by-product.
methods.equipment: מחבת ברזל יצוק / פלנצ'ה כבדה (~₪120-600) + a vessel for the fat
methods.whyItMatters: This is THE method for goose and duck breast, and the model cannot express any of its four defining features: start cold, one side only, pour off mid-cook, and a yield. We have it as `sear:'כן'` plus `mid:'ייבוש'`.
methods.safetyNote: No safety value changes. See the 57°C endpoint note under ברווז — it applies identically to n=9 חזה אווז (tgt 65, doneness mr 57, rare 54, safe 74).

methods.whatItProduces: Stage 1: 135-150°C until the subcutaneous fat has rendered out and the legs reach 82-85°C. Stage 2: 220-230°C or a broiler for 10-15 min to blister and crisp. This resolves the core waterfowl conflict — the meat's ideal endpoint is far BELOW the temperature at which fat renders well.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED) or a lidded grill; a deep drip pan (`drippan` token exists)
methods.whyItMatters: Our model has exactly ONE smoke temperature and one 'grill finish'. It has no concept of a temperature SCHEDULE inside a single method. For waterfowl that schedule is the whole technique.
methods.safetyNote: USDA FSIS 74°C applies to whole goose (poultry). Our n=44 tgt is 74 and safe is 74 — consistent.

methods.whatItProduces: PROCESS STAGE. Uncovered on a rack in the fridge, optionally scalded with boiling water first (Peking method) and/or glazed with maltose/vinegar. Dehydrates the skin so it can shatter rather than leather.
methods.equipment: רשת + תבנית + open fridge space; optionally a small fan
methods.whyItMatters: The highest-leverage skin technique in the domain, and a MULTI-DAY schedule item invisible to the work plan. `mid:'ייבוש'` is a mid-cook note, not a pre-stage.

methods.whatItProduces: Classic German/Chinese goose: steam or covered-with-liquid 45-60 min to render a large volume of fat and pre-tenderise, then roast dry at 200°C+ for colour. Reduces flare-up risk enormously and shortens the dry phase.
methods.equipment: סיר גדול + סל אידוי (~₪150-500), or a covered roasting pan with water; a steam oven if owned (the `steam` bool exists at app.js:98)
methods.whyItMatters: For a 4.5 kg goose this is arguably the safest and most reliable route, and we model the hardware prop (`steam`) with no method to consume it.

methods.whatItProduces: The best whole-waterfowl geometry: rotation drains fat continuously from every surface instead of pooling it on the underside, and self-bastes the skin.
methods.equipment: ערכת רוטיסרי + a heavy motor + a deep drip pan (mandatory — the fat volume is large)
methods.whyItMatters: Prop exists, method does not.
methods.safetyNote: The fire hazard here is real and specific: 0.5-1 kg of rendered fat dripping onto coals. `drippan` is already an equipment token — a fat-heavy method should be able to declare it a HARD requirement, which needs the method vocabulary to exist first.

methods.whatItProduces: Smoked goose breast is excellent; whole goose in a smoker renders slowly and takes deep smoke, but skin stays soft.
methods.equipment: מעשנה (owned) + drip pan
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled, but with no way to require the drip pan or to add the high-heat finish the skin needs.

methods.whatItProduces: Salt-cure a breast 24-36h, rinse, wrap, hang 2-4 weeks. A dry-cured, sliceable charcuterie product — not a cook at all.
methods.equipment: תא ריפוי / ייבוש (`curechamber`, ALREADY an owned equipment token) + `humidity` + `scale` at 0.1g
methods.whyItMatters: We have a full charcuterie apparatus (curechamber, humidity, hooks, rh_pct and hang specs in equipment_map.py) and duck/goose breast is absent from SPECIALS entirely. The gear is modelled; the product is not.
methods.safetyNote: Whole-muscle dry curing of poultry has cure-salt, water-activity and weight-loss controls. I have no primary source that covers poultry (as opposed to pork) whole-muscle dry cure: requires research.

categories.notesOnOurModel: n=48 חזה ברווז has doneness with `mr:57` default and `rare:54`, against `safe:74`. That is a deliberate, culinary-standard deviation from the USDA poultry floor with no pasteurization argument behind it — a 2-minute sear does not deliver a time-temperature lethality. n=46 ברווז שלם and n=47 שוק ברווז (קונפי) have no doneness and fall to the collagen branch, so whole duck defaults to sous-vide+smoke and cannot be roasted; the confit leg cannot be confited. `mid:'חריטת עור'` and `somid:'דקירת עור'` show the engine knows the vocabulary of scoring and piercing but has no stage to run.

methods.whatItProduces: The canonical duck-breast method. Crosshatch, cold dry pan, skin-down, low, 12-15 min, pour off fat 2-3 times, flip 60-90s, rest. Crackling skin, MR (54-57°C) meat, ~100 ml rendered fat.
methods.equipment: מחבת ברזל יצוק / פלנצ'ה (~₪120-600) + fat vessel
methods.whyItMatters: Our model produces the OPPOSITE ordering. The step composer runs prep → sv → smoke → grill-finish → rest, so it will sous-vide the breast to 57°C (leaving the fat entirely unrendered) and then offer a short grill finish that physically cannot render a 6-8 mm fat cap. The correct sequences are render-first-then-SV, or SV-then-long-cold-pan-render. We can express neither.
methods.safetyNote: Duck is a poultry species; USDA FSIS 74°C applies. Our 57°C default is the restaurant standard, not a sourced-safe value. I have NO primary source that legitimises a 57°C duck breast: requires research — and if none exists, this must render as a disclosed chef's deviation, not as a target.

methods.whatItProduces: See אווז. For n=47 specifically: cure 12-24h, submerge in duck fat, 80-85°C for 2-3h, chill under fat, crisp to serve.
methods.equipment: סיר עמוק + ~1 ק"ג שומן ברווז + oven or bath at 80-85°C
methods.whyItMatters: `svt:80/svh:8` is a sous-vide analogue and the honest description of what the app offers. The cure, the fat medium, the storage step and the crisp finish are all absent.
methods.safetyNote: See אווז/CONFIT — no primary source for cure ratio or shelf life: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: PROCESS STAGE, 24-72h. For whole duck the full Peking treatment adds a boiling-water scald and a maltose glaze before drying, which is what makes the skin puff and shatter.
methods.equipment: רשת + תבנית + fridge space; optionally a fan; a kettle for the scald
methods.whyItMatters: Multi-day, schedule-critical, invisible to the orchestrator.

methods.whatItProduces: Whole duck: 150°C until legs reach ~82°C and fat has drained, then 220-230°C for 10-15 min. Crisp skin, cooked legs, no leathered breast.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED) + deep drip pan
methods.whyItMatters: Same structural gap as goose: no temperature schedule inside one method.

methods.whatItProduces: Whole duck on a rack over a deep pan, fat drained off periodically. The domestic default.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED) + רשת + תבנית עמוקה
methods.whyItMatters: n=46 currently cannot be roasted at all — the branch marks a bare grill invalid and defaults to sous-vide a 2.2 kg whole bird.

methods.whatItProduces: Perfect edge-to-edge 57°C breast. Fat completely unrendered; skin flabby.
methods.equipment: סו-ויד + ואקום (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled — but the app presents it as complete when for duck it is only half the technique.

methods.whatItProduces: Tea-smoked / cherry-smoked duck breast; excellent flavour, and at 100°C (our `smt`) the fat begins to render, so smoke here is doing real work.
methods.equipment: מעשנה (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled and genuinely apt for duck breast.

methods.whatItProduces: The finish that rescues sous-vide or braised duck skin: 3-5 min of top-down radiant heat.
methods.equipment: תנור top element; `torch` (owned) is the small-scale substitute
methods.whyItMatters: Named, bounded, one-sided high heat — the model has only 'grill', which implies a grate and two sides.

categories.notesOnOurModel: All 5 have doneness, so all sit in the steak-like branch where every combination including a bare grill is legal. Three structural gaps. (1) WHOLE vs FILLET does not exist: n=50 פורל is a 0.4 kg whole fish and n=49 סלמון is a 1 kg fillet, and the model cannot distinguish them — yet whole fish enables salt crust, stuffing, and clamp-grilling while fillets do not. (2) COLD SMOKE exists ONLY inside the MAKE profile 'דג מעושן' (app.js:3722, '≤25°C, 5h, ללא בישול') and is unreachable from any CUT. (3) n=49's `rub` reads 'מלח+סוכר חום (גרבלקס)' — a 2-3 day cure written into a seasoning string, with no ratio, no weight, no press and no yield. n=125 טונה has `somid:'סושי-גרייד; מרכז נא'` and tgt 45°C with no parasite-control stage anywhere.

methods.whatItProduces: Flaky, opaque, cooked, smoke-saturated fish. Requires a PELLICLE first — 2-4h of air-drying after the brine — or the smoke will not adhere and the surface weeps albumin.
methods.equipment: מעשנה (owned) at a LOW setting; our `smt:80` is at the bottom of most smokers' controllable range
methods.whyItMatters: The heat method is modelled; the mandatory pellicle stage is not (the glossary at data.py:205 defines 'Pellicle' — the concept is documented and unexecutable).
methods.safetyNote: Fish held for hours between 4°C and 60°C in a low-oxygen smoke atmosphere is the classic Clostridium botulinum type E scenario — type E is cold-tolerant and aquatic in origin. The controlling document is the FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance (4th ed.), smoked-fish / C. botulinum chapter. The specific water-phase-salt %, nitrite ppm and time limits: requires research — do not ship numbers without the verbatim text.

methods.whatItProduces: Smoke flavour and colour with NO cooking. Texture stays raw-silky and translucent; the product is lox/Nova, not smoked fish. Chamber must stay low (commonly cited ≤30°C) or the protein sets and the product is ruined.
methods.equipment: מחולל עישון קר — a maze or tube pellet smoker (~₪80-300) placed in an UNHEATED chamber; ambient temperature is the limiting factor in Israel, so this is a winter/night technique or needs ice
methods.whyItMatters: The flagship gap of the fish domain. It is a genuinely different PROCESS — no lethality step, product is ready-to-eat — and it is the gateway to lox, smoked trout, and (for the גבינה category) smoked cheese.
methods.safetyNote: This is the highest-risk method in my domains. Cold-smoked fish receives no kill step and is a ready-to-eat food: the two named hazards are C. botulinum type E toxin formation and Listeria monocytogenes. The authority is the FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance (4th ed.). Every number — the ≤30°C ceiling, the required water-phase salt, the refrigerated shelf life — requires research and must be quoted, never inferred.

methods.whatItProduces: Salt+sugar (roughly equal parts by weight) + dill, pressed under weight, 24-72h in the fridge, liquid poured off. Firms and seasons the flesh, drops water activity, turns it translucent-jewel. Not cooked. Weight loss ~10-15%.
methods.equipment: משקל דיגיטלי (owned) + a non-reactive tray + a weight/press + fridge space
methods.whyItMatters: n=49's rub field names it and nothing executes it. It is also the PREREQUISITE stage for cold-smoked lox — cure first, then smoke — so shipping COLD_SMOKE without CURE would be shipping the dangerous half.
methods.safetyNote: Cure ratio and duration are safety-relevant here, not merely culinary — they are the hurdle. Also: FDA Food Code §3-402.11 requires a freezing step for parasite destruction in fish served raw or undercooked (commonly cited as -20°C/7 days or -35°C/15h), with named species exemptions. Both the schedule and the exemption list: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Soaked untreated cedar/alder plank over indirect heat. The plank smoulders, giving gentle aromatic smoke and steam from below; the fish never touches metal so it cannot stick or break; no flipping; moist, faintly smoky, evenly cooked.
methods.equipment: קרשי ארז/אלמון לגריל (~₪20-60, semi-disposable) + a lidded grill or oven
methods.whyItMatters: The classic salmon-fillet method and the answer to the delicate-fish-sticks-to-the-grate problem. Cheapest missing capability in the whole report.

methods.whatItProduces: Parchment or foil parcel, oven 180-200°C, 12-18 min. Self-steaming in its own moisture plus aromatics. Zero browning, essentially impossible to dry out, sauce forms in the parcel.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED) + נייר אפייה או רדיד (`foil` is an owned token)
methods.whyItMatters: The most forgiving fish method there is — exactly what a beginner-level user (the app has a `lvl-beg` density mode) should be offered, and it is unavailable.

methods.whatItProduces: Whole fish encased in ~2 kg of coarse salt bound with egg white, oven 200°C. The crust becomes a sealed vessel: the fish steams in its own juices, cooks with unusual evenness, and is seasoned only at the skin. Dramatic tableside cracking.
methods.equipment: תנור (OWNED) + ~2 ק"ג מלח גס + a tray; WHOLE fish only
methods.whyItMatters: Requires the whole-vs-fillet distinction our data does not carry. Also a rare case where the DOSE of an ingredient (2 kg of salt) is an equipment-scale concern.

methods.whatItProduces: Whole scored fish held in a hinged basket over embers: crisp blistered skin, smoky, flipped as one unit without disintegrating.
methods.equipment: סלסלת דג / מלחציים (~₪40-150) + גריל (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: 'grill' is modelled but the accessory that makes it POSSIBLE for delicate whole fish is not, so we offer an operation that will physically destroy a 400 g trout on a bare grate.

methods.whatItProduces: Cantonese whole fish: 8-12 min over boiling water, then hot oil and soy poured over. Silky, clean-flavoured, absolutely moist; no colour.
methods.equipment: סיר + סל אידוי / ווק (~₪150-500), or a steam oven (the `steam` prop exists)
methods.whyItMatters: A dominant world method for whole fish, entirely absent.

methods.whatItProduces: Submerged in olive oil at 45-55°C. Extraordinarily silky tuna or salmon; the classic 'confit tuna'. Very close in outcome to sous-vide but with fat-borne flavour.
methods.equipment: סיר + 1-2 ל' שמן זית + probe (owned); or the sous-vide bath with oil in the bag
methods.whyItMatters: Achievable via our owned sous-vide, but the model has no way to say the MEDIUM is oil rather than water — and the medium is what distinguishes the result.
methods.safetyNote: Low-temperature oil holding is a low-oxygen environment; the same C. botulinum considerations as sous-vide apply and Baldwin's fish pasteurization table (55-60°C) is the reference we already carry in docs/sources/baldwin-backbone.md. Whether 45-55°C ever pasteurizes: it does not — this is a hold-and-serve-immediately technique. Needs an explicit sourced statement: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: Salmon/trout skin-down under light pressure in a hot pan, 80% of the cook on the skin side. Shatter-crisp skin, barely-set flesh. The restaurant default.
methods.equipment: מחבת כבדה / פלנצ'ה
methods.whyItMatters: `sear:'לא'` on both n=49 and n=50 — our data actively says do not sear these, which is wrong for the single most common preparation of salmon.

methods.whatItProduces: No cooking. n=125 טונה is already described in our own data as 'סושי-גרייד; מרכז נא' with tgt 45°C.
methods.equipment: סכין חדה + freezer capable of the parasite-control schedule
methods.whyItMatters: We already ship an item whose stated target (45°C) is below any cooking threshold, with no RAW method and no parasite-control stage attached.
methods.safetyNote: FDA Food Code §3-402.11 parasite-destruction freezing (temperature × time) plus the species exemptions (certain large tuna) is the controlling text. Numbers: requires research — quote, do not infer.

methods.whatItProduces: Fish jerky / dried fish. Low heat + airflow over many hours.
methods.equipment: מייבש — ALREADY an option of the `curechamber` prop (app.js:7655), or a low oven
methods.whyItMatters: The hardware is in the equipment vocabulary; no fish method can reach it.

categories.notesOnOurModel: Our third-largest category and the worst fit for the model. It is really FOUR groups flattened into one `cat`: shrimp/prawns (113,114,115,119), large crustaceans (117,118,120,121,122), bivalves (116,128,129,130) and cephalopods (123,124). Two concrete defects. (1) Five items — 120 סרטן כחול, 121 רגלי סרטן, 122 סרטן רך, 128 מולים, 129 קלאמס, 130 אויסטרים — carry `svt=0` yet all have `doneness`, so methodRules puts them in the steak-like branch with `def:['sv','smoke']`: the app's default recommendation for a blue crab is to sous-vide it at 0°C. (2) The truth is written into free-text fields the engine cannot act on: `sear` reads 'הרתחה/אידוי' (boil/steam), 'צריבה/טיגון' (sear/fry), 'הרתחה→גריל' (boil→grill) — three real methods stored as strings inside a boolean-ish field. Third, and deepest: FIVE of these items are done when the SHELL OPENS, not at a probe temperature. You cannot probe a mussel. Assigning n=128 מולים `doneness:{med:63, well:68}` describes a measurement nobody will ever take, and our whole doneness/probe architecture is inapplicable to a third of this category.

methods.whatItProduces: Rolling seasoned water or court-bouillon. THE primary method for blue crab, whole lobster, shrimp boils and langoustine. Even, fast, fully-cooked, seasoned through the shell; no browning at all. Doneness by shell colour and time, not by probe.
methods.equipment: סיר גדול 15-20 ל' (~₪150-500) + a burner that can hold a rolling boil
methods.whyItMatters: For n=118 לובסטר שלם and n=120 סרטן כחול this is the world-default preparation, and our data KNOWS it — `sear:'גריל/הרתחה'` and `sear:'הרתחה/אידוי'` — but stores it where nothing reads it. This is the single most-used missing method in the category.
methods.safetyNote: FDA guidance for crab/lobster is cook until the flesh is opaque and reaches 63°C/145°F — this is already correctly cited in sources.py ('FDA — cook crab until internal 145°F/63°C and flesh opaque'). The authority exists; only the METHOD is missing.

methods.whatItProduces: Above the water, lid on. Primary method for mussels, clams, king crab legs and Maryland-style blue crab. Gentler than boiling, does not waterlog or leach flavour, and produces a concentrated liquor as a by-product. Doneness signal for bivalves is the shell opening (~5-7 min).
methods.equipment: סיר גדול + סל אידוי (~₪150-500); a lidded grill can substitute with a covered pan
methods.whyItMatters: Covers 6 of the 15 items as their PRIMARY method. Currently they default to sous-vide at 0°C.
methods.safetyNote: FDA: cook shellfish until the shells open; discard any that do not open. Our sources.py already carries this ('cook shellfish until shells open'). We also need the pre-cook rule (live bivalves only; discard any that are gaping and do not close when tapped) — I do not have that clause verbatim: requires research.

methods.whatItProduces: THE scallop method: patted bone-dry, ripping-hot pan, 90-120 s per side, do not move it. Deep hazelnut crust over a translucent barely-set centre. Full-contact conduction — a grate cannot do this because it only touches in stripes.
methods.equipment: מחבת ברזל יצוק / פלנצ'ה (~₪150-600). 'פלנצ׳ה / פלטה' already exists as a grill TYPE in app.js:80.
methods.whyItMatters: n=116 סקלופס has `sear:'צריבה'` and `somid:'יבשים! 2-3 דק'/צד, אל תזיז'` — the technique is written out in full, in Hebrew, in a note field, and the engine offers 'grill' instead. Also the correct method for n=122 סרטן רך.
methods.safetyNote: FDA cooked seafood 63°C/145°F — already cited in sources.py for scallops. Scallops are conventionally served translucent below that; that deviation is disclosed by our doneness ladder (mr 52°C) and should stay disclosed.

methods.whatItProduces: The entire culinary point of octopus. Stage 1: 45-90 min of gentle simmer, braise, pressure or sous-vide to hydrolyse a very high collagen load. Stage 2: 2-4 min of violent direct char. Outcome: yielding-tender interior with a blistered, smoky, crisp exterior. Skip stage 1 and you get a rubber eraser; skip stage 2 and you get boiled octopus.
methods.equipment: סיר / סיר לחץ / סו-ויד (owned) for stage 1 + גריל (owned) for stage 2
methods.whyItMatters: n=123 תמנון encodes this three times in prose (`svt:77/5h`, `sear:'הרתחה→גריל'`, `somid:'בשל 45-60 דק' לריכוך ואז חריכה'`) and zero times in the engine. Worse: because n=123 has `doneness`, it lands in the steak-like branch where a BARE `['grill']` is a legal combination — the app will cheerfully offer grill-only for octopus, which is the one thing that cannot work. This is the clearest case in my domains for a MANDATORY-SEQUENCE construct (`require` exists in methodRules for gizzards; it needs an ordered-pair form).

methods.whatItProduces: Bivalves straight onto direct heat, cupped side down so the liquor is retained; they pop open when done (5-10 min) and self-baste in their own hot brine. The SHELL is the cooking vessel. Smoky, briny, minimal handling.
methods.equipment: גריל (owned) + מלקחיים (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled only as generic 'grill'. The distinguishing feature — doneness signalled by a mechanical event rather than a temperature — has no representation, which is why n=130 אויסטרים carries a doneness ladder (63/68°C) that describes an impossible measurement. A DONENESS_SIGNAL field ('shell opens' | 'flesh opaque' | 'shell bright red' | 'probe °C') would fix this across 6 items.
methods.safetyNote: FDA: cook until shells open; discard unopened. Already cited in sources.py.

methods.whatItProduces: 180°C oil. THE method for soft-shell crab (eaten whole, shatter-crisp) and for calamari rings. 60-180 seconds. No other method produces that exterior.
methods.equipment: מטגנת / סיר כבד + 2-3 ל' שמן + מדחום (`probe` owned) (~₪200-700)
methods.whyItMatters: n=122 סרטן רך's `rub` field literally reads 'קמח+פפריקה (טיגון)' — flour and paprika, FOR FRYING — and `sear:'צריבה/טיגון'`. Our own data specifies a dredge for a method we do not have.
methods.safetyNote: FDA cooked seafood 63°C/145°F applies. Oil-temperature control is a quality not safety matter here.

methods.whatItProduces: Hard fast char. Correct for shrimp (skewered so they cannot curl and can be turned as one unit), split lobster tail flesh-down first, and squid at 30-60 s per side.
methods.equipment: גריל (owned) + שיפודים
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled and dominant here. What is lost is the SKEWER and the shell-on/peeled decision, both of which change the outcome materially — shell-on shrimp stay far juicier, which our own n=114 note says ('בקליפה לעסיסיות').

methods.whatItProduces: Lobster tail at 54-57°C in butter: the texture that made this technique famous — silky, never rubbery, impossible to hit by boiling. Also excellent for octopus stage 1.
methods.equipment: סו-ויד + ואקום (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: The bath is modelled; the butter medium is not — same medium-blindness as the fish oil-poach. And the default `['sv','smoke']` applies sous-vide indiscriminately to five items with `svt=0`, which discredits the recommendation where it is genuinely brilliant.

methods.whatItProduces: ~120°C wet heat: octopus tender in 15-20 min instead of 60-90. Also the fastest crustacean-shell stock.
methods.equipment: סיר לחץ (~₪250-800), not owned
methods.whyItMatters: Turns the octopus two-stage from a 2-hour project into a 30-minute one — a large orchestrator win.

methods.whatItProduces: Genuinely good on oysters, mussels and shrimp (minutes, not hours). Marginal-to-wrong on crab and lobster, where the shell blocks smoke and the flesh dries.
methods.equipment: מעשנה (owned)
methods.whyItMatters: Modelled, but it is in the DEFAULT combination for all 15 items including whole crab, which is bad advice presented as the recommendation.

methods.whatItProduces: No cooking at all — the single most common way oysters are consumed. Shucked, served on ice with mignonette.
methods.equipment: סכין צדפות + כפפת הגנה (neither modelled)
methods.whyItMatters: n=130 אויסטרים is in the catalog with only cooked routes.
methods.safetyNote: Raw oysters carry a Vibrio vulnificus / parahaemolyticus risk with a specific at-risk-population advisory (liver disease, immunocompromised, pregnancy). sources.py already flags 'raw oysters carry Vibrio risk'. The FDA advisory text and the at-risk list: requires research — this method must not ship without it.

methods.whatItProduces: Very high heat, constant motion, 60-120 s. Squid and shrimp specifically: wok hei, slight char, still tender.
methods.equipment: ווק + a high-output burner (~₪150-600)
methods.whyItMatters: A major world method for exactly the items in this category that overcook fastest.

missingEquipment.unlocks: COLD_SMOKE — lox/Nova from cured salmon, cold-smoked trout; and outside my domain, cold-smoked cheese for the 33-item גבינה category. Turns any unheated box into a cold smoker.
PRESSURE_COOK — octopus stage 1 in 15-20 min instead of 60-90; turkey legs and wings to shreddable in ~25 min; crustacean stock.
ROTISSERIE for every whole bird and for hanging shawarma. NOTE: the grill `rotisserie` boolean prop ALREADY EXISTS at app.js:89 — we ask the user if they own it and never use the answer.
BOIL and STEAM — the primary method for 6 of the 15 seafood items (blue crab, whole lobster, king crab legs, mussels, clams, shrimp boil).

missingEquipment.equipment: Deep fryer or heavy pot + oil thermometer
missingEquipment.unlocks: DEEP_FRY — soft-shell crab, calamari, chicken wings. A dedicated 30-40 L turkey fryer is a separate, higher-risk purchase.

SCORE_AND_RENDER (cold-pan duck and goose breast) and PAN_SEAR (scallops, salmon skin-down, soft-shell crab). NOTE: 'פלנצ׳ה / פלטה' already exists as a grill TYPE at app.js:80, but it is modelled as a grill and behaves like a griddle.
Whole-fish grilling without disintegration — makes an existing modelled method (grill) actually viable for a 400 g trout.
PLANK — the classic salmon method: gentle indirect heat, aromatic smoke, no sticking, no flip. Cheapest capability in this list.
VERTICAL_ROAST — upright geometry, fat drains down, all skin faces the heat.

missingEquipment.equipment: Wire rack + rimmed sheet pan (dedicated to uncovered fridge drying)
missingEquipment.unlocks: BRINE_DRY and AIR_DRY_UNCOVERED — the highest-leverage skin technique across all four poultry/waterfowl categories, and the multi-day stage the orchestrator most needs to see.

missingEquipment.equipment: Brining container / food-grade bucket with fridge space
missingEquipment.hebrewName: כלי כבישה / דלי מזון + מקום במקרר
missingEquipment.unlocks: BRINE_WET for turkey and chicken. The binding constraint is refrigerated volume, which is a real spec the equipment model could carry.
CONFIT (duck and goose legs, plus ~1-2 kg of rendered fat as an input) and OVEN_BRAISE (turkey legs and wings).
WOK_STIR_FRY — squid, shrimp, chicken breast strips.
AIR_FRY — wings and drumsticks, the everyday consumer route the app cannot mention.
DEHYDRATE — fish jerky, turkey jerky. NOTE: 'מייבש' ALREADY exists as an option of the `curechamber` prop at app.js:7655 — hardware modelled, method absent.
RAW_HALF_SHELL for oysters, and pre-shucking for grilled scallops.
STEAM_THEN_ROAST (goose), STEAM (whole fish), and controlled-humidity roasting. NOTE: the oven `steam` boolean prop ALREADY EXISTS at app.js:98 with no consumer.

crossCuttingFindings:
SIX structural patterns, ordered by how much they should shape the vocabulary's SHAPE rather than its length.

(1) A METHOD IS A POINT IN AN OUTCOME SPACE, NOT A NAME. Every method in my 37 items resolves to five independent axes: MEDIUM (dry air / steam / water / fat / vacuum-water / oil-bath / smoke), HEAT DIRECTION (all-round / one-sided / rotating / top-down / full-contact conduction), SURFACE RESULT (shatter-crisp / crackling / pellicle / opaque-no-colour / char), INTERIOR RESULT (silky / juicy / flaky / shreddable / rubbery-risk), and SMOKE LEVEL (none / cold / light / heavy). Model methods as points in that space and two things fall out for free: substitution advice ("no rotisserie? indirect grill, flip every 20 min — you lose evenness, you keep the skin") and honest warnings ("sous-vide duck gives you the interior axis and costs you the surface axis"). Model them as a flat list of names and you get another enum that will be wrong for the next 130 items.

(2) THE MISSING HEAT SOURCES ARE THE COMMON ONES. Not exotic gear — a dry oven (owned, with `fan` and `steam` props already modelled) and a pot of water. Across my 37 items, boiling or steaming is the PRIMARY method for 6 seafood items, oven roasting for all 6 whole/large birds, and pan/plancha searing for scallops, soft-shell crab, salmon skin-down and both waterfowl breasts. The three-method model does not describe a subset of cooking; it describes a barbecue.

(3) THE MODEL HAS NO PRE-COOK AND NO POST-COOK STAGE, AND THIS IS AN ORCHESTRATOR APP. Thaw (3 days for a turkey), wet brine (4-12h), dry brine (24-72h), cure (24-72h for gravlax), air-dry/pellicle (2-72h), score, spatchcock, purge, tenderise. All are real, all consume clock time, all are currently smuggled into `rub`, `mid`, `sear` and `somid` as Hebrew prose. The work plan cannot schedule what it cannot see. `kg` is already stored, so thaw time is arithmetic we are not doing.

(4) DONENESS IS NOT ALWAYS A TEMPERATURE. Six of my items are done by a mechanical or visual SIGNAL: the shell opens (mussels, clams, oysters), the shell turns bright red (blue crab), the flesh turns opaque (crab, shrimp), 30-60 seconds a side (squid). Our architecture assumes a probe target everywhere, so n=128 מולים carries `doneness:{med:63,well:68}` — a measurement no one will ever take on a mussel. A `donenessSignal` discriminator alongside the temperature ladder fixes this for a fifth of my domain.

(5) ONE ITEM CAN HAVE TWO TARGETS. A whole bird's breast wants ~63°C and its thigh wants 74-82°C. That divergence IS the technique — it is why spatchcocking, rotisserie, breast-shielding, ice-packing and cook-the-parts-separately all exist. Our one-item-one-`tgt` schema cannot state the central fact about the four whole birds in my domains, and consequently cannot explain why any of the techniques exist.

(6) A METHOD CAN BE A SEQUENCE WITH A MANDATORY ORDER, OR A TEMPERATURE RAMP. Octopus is tenderise-THEN-char (reverse it and you get a rubber eraser; today a bare `['grill']` is a legal combination for it). Duck is render-THEN-cook or cook-THEN-render, and our composer's fixed order (prep → sv → smoke → grill → rest) is exactly wrong for it. Whole goose is 150°C-THEN-230°C. `methodRules` has `require` and `invalid` but no ordered-pair or ramp construct.

TWO LIVE DEFECTS, not vocabulary gaps, that a reader should not lose in the above: (a) the six doneness-less items — n=3 שווארמה, 43 הודו שלם, 44 אווז שלם, 45 שוק אווז, 46 ברווז שלם, 47 שוק ברווז — fall through methodRules' final "collagen/long cuts" branch, so a 6 kg whole turkey defaults to sous-vide and roasting or grilling it alone is marked invalid; (b) five items with `svt=0` (120, 121, 122, 128, 129, 130) still receive `def:['sv','smoke']`, so the app recommends sous-vide at 0°C for a blue crab.

AND A REPEATED INERT-SHIPMENT PATTERN: we already model `rotisserie` (app.js:89), oven `fan` and `steam` (app.js:97-98), the grill types 'פלנצ׳ה / פלטה' and 'לבה / אינפרא' (app.js:80), grill `lid` and `zones`, `drippan`, and 'מייבש' as a curechamber kind (app.js:7655). Every one of these is a capability we ask the user about, store, and can never consume — because no method exists that reads it. The hardware vocabulary is already ahead of the method vocabulary; the gap is not in the equipment model.
researchNeeded: FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance, 4th ed. — the smoked-fish / Clostridium botulinum toxin-formation chapter, VERBATIM: required water-phase salt % in the finished product, nitrite ppm where used, maximum process temperature, refrigerated shelf life, and the distinct requirements for hot- vs cold-smoked. Blocks COLD_SMOKE and constrains our existing fish `smt:80`. Highest-risk item in this report.

FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance — the Listeria monocytogenes control expectations for cold-smoked (ready-to-eat, no-lethality-step) fish. COLD_SMOKE must not ship without this.

An authority for the cold-smoking ambient temperature ceiling (commonly cited as ≤30°C / ≤86°F). Our MAKE_COOK profile already prints '≤25°C' with no source behind it — either find the source or stop printing the number.

FDA Food Code §3-402.11 — the parasite-destruction freezing schedule for fish served raw or undercooked (temperature × time, e.g. the -20°C/7-day and -35°C/15h routes), PLUS the species exemption list (large tuna). Blocks RAW_CRUDO and gravlax; n=125 טונה already ships with tgt 45°C and 'סושי-גרייד' text and no control.

USDA FSIS — refrigerator thawing time per unit weight for whole poultry, and the prohibition on counter thawing. We store `kg`; this converts directly into a multi-day work-plan stage for n=43 הודו שלם.
USDA FSIS — the requirement that STUFFING inside a bird reach 74°C / 165°F, verbatim. We have no field for a secondary thermal mass.

USDA FSIS — whether the 74°C / 165°F poultry floor is stated to apply to duck and goose, and whether any FSIS or Baldwin time-temperature route legitimises a 57°C duck/goose breast. We ship `tgt:57, rare:54` against `safe:74` on n=48 and n=9. If no source blesses it, it must render as a disclosed chef's deviation, never as a recommended target.

Baldwin — poultry pasteurization time-at-temperature at 57-65°C indexed BY THICKNESS, applied to (a) duck/goose breast geometry and (b) a spatchcocked bird. We carry his backbone table in docs/sources/baldwin-backbone.md but not thickness-indexed values for these shapes.

Baldwin — fish pasteurization at 50-60°C by thickness, applied to our own stated values: does salmon at `svt:50 / svh:0.75` actually pasteurize a 1 kg fillet, or are we shipping a hold-and-serve-immediately technique labelled as a cook?

FDA / national shellfish sanitation guidance — live-bivalve acceptance rules BEFORE cooking (discard gaping shells that do not close when tapped) and the discard-unopened-after-cooking rule, verbatim. Our sources.py has the post-cook half only.
FDA raw-molluscan-shellfish advisory — the Vibrio vulnificus / parahaemolyticus statement and the at-risk population list. Blocks RAW_HALF_SHELL for n=130 אויסטרים.

USDA FSIS and/or NFPA turkey deep-frying safety guidance — oil-volume displacement, fully-thawed-only, outdoor-only siting. Blocks DEEP_FRY at whole-bird scale; this is the highest-consequence operation named anywhere in this report.

Confit: a primary source for the salt-cure ratio and duration, whether an 80-90°C fat hold constitutes a pasteurizing process for poultry legs, and the refrigerated shelf life of a product stored under a fat seal. I have NO source for any of these three and they are all safety-relevant. Blocks CONFIT for n=45 and n=47.

Whole-muscle DRY-CURED poultry (duck/goose breast 'prosciutto') — cure-salt type and dose, target water activity or weight-loss %, and drying conditions. All our existing charcuterie citations are pork; poultry is a different risk profile. Blocks adding cured duck breast to SPECIALS.

Convection (fan) roasting — a citable source for the temperature/time relationship versus conventional (commonly stated as -20°C and shorter). Needed only if OVEN_ROAST computes times rather than stating a range; we already model the oven `fan` prop.

A safety-relevant statement on brining temperature: brine and dry-brine stages must be held at refrigeration temperature for their full duration (12-72h). Cite the USDA FSIS cold-holding clause verbatim before shipping BRINE_WET or BRINE_DRY as scheduled stages.
